title: O Spirit, Freed from Earth
description: O Spirit, Freed from Earth in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Mary Howitt wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 351, “He is Risen”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O spir-it, freed from earth, Re-joice, thy work is done! The wea-ry world's be-neath thy feet, Thou bright-er than the sun!

lines: The weary world's beneath thy feet,
Now sorrow hath no part in thee,
Awake to love which knows no change,
Thou who hast done with time!
Thou, who hast done with tears.
The living God hath touched thy lips,
Thou who hast done with earth!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Mary Howitt died in 1888.
credits: Words by Mary Howitt (1799–1888), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
